description:
THE STAGGER STOPS BEING A CUTSCENE. ONE INSTRUCTION, THREE BYTES. This is the pack to test FIRST for the "I get tackled and then I can't do anything" complaint. It does NOT reduce contact - nothing here changes how often anyone is knocked about. It removes the veto that stops you acting while the knock-about animation plays.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG (the explanation). Every animated action in this game is an object with two gates. match::anime::action::<X>::vf2(this, animePlayer) answers "may I START, given what this player is doing right now?", and it decides by switching on the CURRENT action's kind byte at animePlayer+0xad0. For a few current kinds it says yes outright; for a few more it delegates to the CURRENT action's vf14, "may I be interrupted?"; for everything else it says NO and the request dies there. match::anime::action::Stagger::vf14 is 0x143f00de0 and it answers by comparing the animation's CURRENT FRAME against a key frame pulled out of the stagger animation's own event data (event type 5). Emulated on the game's own bytes: it returns 1 only when currentFrame >= keyFrame AND keyFrame > 0. IF THE STAGGER ANIMATION CARRIES NO TYPE-5 CANCEL EVENT, keyFrame IS 0 AND THE ANSWER IS NO FOR EVERY FRAME OF THE ANIMATION - the stagger is literally uninterruptible until it ends by itself. That is the canned animation you are watching.

WHAT CHANGES. Stagger::vf14 initialises its refuse return value with 'xor dil,dil' at 0x143f00e03 and that register is the answer on every path that does not explicitly set it. This pack changes that one instruction to 'mov dil,1' - same three bytes - so the answer is YES for the whole stagger, from frame 0, regardless of what the animation data says.

WHAT IT DOES AND DOES NOT GIVE YOU. Only actions whose own vf2 DELEGATES to the current action can benefit. Emulated over the whole action set with the current action set to Stagger (kind 0x10): Dribble (kind 4) and Trap (kind 7) delegate; Move, Feint, Dodge, Sliding, Tackle, Jostle, Reaction, Block and the Contact family are refused by their OWN vf2 before Stagger::vf14 is ever asked. So with this pack alone: if you still have the ball you can dribble out of a stagger immediately, and with or without the ball you can reach for / trap a loose ball immediately. YOU STILL CANNOT SIMPLY RUN out of a stagger - plain locomotion is kind 2 and Move::vf2 refuses outright while a Stagger is current. That is what contact-move-out-of-stagger.json is for; test this one on its own first.

HOW IT WAS DEMONSTRATED (a-EMULATED, this pass). Stagger::vf14 was run under Unicorn on the INSTALLED image with its six anime-data callees stubbed (0x143e940a0 motion handle, 0x143e9a390 event count, 0x143e99b70 / 0x143e99e20 / 0x143e9b220 key frame, 0x143ea9040 current frame, 0x14533ea80 float helper) and the flag-bit helpers at 0x1443110xx-0x1443123xx left to run for real. Requesting kinds {Move, Dribble, Trap, Sliding, Tackle, Block, Stagger, Feint, Reaction, Dodge, Jostle, GK-Catch} x currentFrame {0,10,19,20,40} with keyFrame 20: STOCK returns 0 for every kind at frames 0/10/19 and 1 at frames 20/40. With keyFrame 0 (no cancel event): STOCK returns 0 at frames 0, 10, 40 AND 120 - never. WITH THIS PATCH: 1 in every one of those cases. The requesting kind changes only WHICH key frame index is looked up (kind 4 uses the LAST type-5 event when the animation has two or more; the GK save family takes a separate branch); it never changes the comparison.

WHO IT AFFECTS: EVERYONE, identically - your stick-controlled player, your AI team-mates and the CPU. Stagger::vf14 reads only the motion id, the anime key frames, the current frame and the requesting action's kind. It does not read any "is this player human-controlled" flag, and no RTTI-named method in match::pad:: or match::ai:: reads the current action kind at all. The lock is not a human-only lock and lifting it is not a human-only buff.

IT DOES NOT REDUCE CONTACT. No collision test, no contact score, no stagger-versus-falldown decision and no foul term is touched. Keep falls-slide-tackle-contact.json and the rest of the falls set - this pack is the other half of that trade: MORE contact events, SHORTER agency locks.

DO NOT APPLY falls-stagger-lock-balance.json ALONGSIDE THIS. That pack was written to make staggers cost MORE time (6.0 -> 8.0 on a different function, Stagger::vf32) and is aimed the opposite way to this one.

EXPECTED EFFECT ON FOULS AND CARDS: NONE. The foul model (scorer 0x143d88fe0, level function 0x143d861f0, thresholds 40/60/80/110) is computed from collision geometry before any reaction is chosen and is never read by Stagger::vf14.

WHAT TO LOOK FOR IN ONE MATCH. Get shoulder-barged or clipped while on the ball and try to keep going: stock you watch, with this you should be able to push the ball on out of the stumble. Also watch loose balls after contact - you should be able to stretch for them mid-stagger instead of after.

WHAT WOULD MEAN IT IS TOO STRONG. Staggers that end the instant they start, so contact looks weightless and players snap out of animations - that reads on screen as a skip rather than a stumble. Also: a ball-carrier who is untouchable because every knock is cancelled on frame 0. If you see either, pull this pack; it cannot be softened - a gentler version would mean moving the key frame in the animation data, which nobody has decoded.

COLLISIONS: none. 0x143f00e03 is byte-identical in the INSTALLED image and in eFootball.exe.PRISTINE (both 4032FF, verified this pass). It is not in the already-applied kick-error bytes (0x14401b423, 0x14401a12c, 0x1440187b4, 0x14105ed1e) and does not overlap any other spec. falls-stagger-lock-balance touches Stagger::vf32 (0x143f00af8) and falls-ballhit-severity / falls-stagger-angle touch Stagger::vf30 (0x143effd70..), all different functions.

REVERT: python tools/exe_patch.py remove tools/data/patches/contact-stagger-interrupt-open.json

patches.name: a staggering player is no longer immune to starting a new action
patches.note: xor dil,dil -> mov dil,1. Same length. dil is the refuse default returned by Stagger::vf14 (0x143f00de0); it is written once here and read once at 0x143f00ed4 ('movzx eax,dil'), the single return path for every branch except the 0x143f00f6d shortcut which already returns 1. Forcing it to 1 makes the function return 1 unconditionally. Site byte-identical in PRISTINE and the installed exe.
